problem_statement: Aggregated LLM leaderboards obscure prompt- and user-specific performance variations; stratified evaluation is data-prohibitive for fine-grained tasks.
core_contributions: Introduces Prompt-to-Leaderboard (P2L), a method that generates prompt-specific leaderboards using LLMs to predict Bradley-Terry coefficients from natural language prompts.
Enables unsupervised, fine-grained evaluation without requiring prompt-stratified human voting data — overcoming data scarcity for niche tasks (e.g., SQL queries).
Demonstrates power-law scaling of prompt-specific evaluation capability with model size and data, and deploys a P2L-based router achieving #1 on Chatbot Arena in Jan 2025.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on pairwise human preference data (e.g., Chatbot Arena); assumes prompt space is meaningfully embeddable; performance on out-of-distribution prompts is reasonable but not robustly generalizable per Section 3.6.

evidence_spans.claim_value: P2L produces leaderboards specific to a prompt by training an LLM to output Bradley-Terry coefficients
evidence_spans.evidence_text: The core idea is to train an LLM taking natural language prompts as input to output a vector of Bradley-Terry coefficients which are then used to predict the human preference vote.

evidence_spans.claim_value: P2L enables unsupervised task-specific evaluation and optimal routing
evidence_spans.evidence_text: The resulting prompt-dependent leaderboards allow for unsupervised task-specific evaluation, optimal routing of queries to models, personalization, and automated evaluation of model strengths and weaknesses.

evidence_spans.claim_value: A P2L-based router achieved #1 on Chatbot Arena in January 2025
evidence_spans.evidence_text: In January 2025, the router we trained based on this methodology achieved the #1 spot in the Chatbot Arena leaderboard.

evidence_spans.claim_value: P2L avoids impractical data requirements of stratified BT regression
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Finer-grained categories, for example SQL table joins, would demand even more data, making stratified regression impractical and slow. And the finest-grained analyses—for example, producing leaderboards for a specific prompt or use-case—are rendered impossible.

problem_statement: Large vocabulary size (e.g., 128k–152k tokens) degrades speculative sampling efficiency due to excessive LM head computation during draft token selection, limiting speed gains despite lightweight draft models.
core_contributions: Introduces FR-Spec, a frequency-ranked vocabulary compression strategy for speculative sampling to reduce LM head computation overhead by 75%
Demonstrates 1.12× average speedup over EAGLE-2 on large-vocabulary LLMs (e.g., Llama-3-8B with 128k tokens)
Provides a plug-and-play enhancement compatible with existing speculative sampling methods (e.g., EAGLE-2, Medusa) without retraining
limitations_or_scope: Focused on speculative sampling acceleration; assumes token frequency statistics are stable and representative; does not address draft model architecture redesign or training dynamics.

evidence_spans.claim_value: FR-Spec reduces LM Head computation overhead by 75%
evidence_spans.evidence_text: By constraining the draft search to a frequency-prioritized token subset, our method reduces LM Head computation overhead by 75% while ensuring the equivalence of the final output distribution.
Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate an average of 1.12× speedup over the state-of-the-art speculative sampling method EAGLE-2.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Compatible with existing methods without retraining
evidence_spans.evidence_text: FR-Spec can be applied to most existing speculative sampling methods with one-click modification and requires no retraining.

problem_statement: LLMs lack reliable, proactive question-asking under uncertainty—especially critical in high-stakes expert domains like clinical reasoning where effective information-gathering directly impacts diagnostic accuracy and safety.
core_contributions: Introduces Alfa, a theory-grounded framework for aligning LLMs to ask high-quality follow-up questions via fine-grained attribute decomposition (e.g., clarity, diagnostic relevance, medical accuracy)
Releases MediQ-AskDocs: a new dataset of 17k clinical interactions and 80k expert-annotated, attribute-specific preference pairs for question-asking evaluation
Demonstrates 56.6% reduction in diagnostic errors and 64.4% question-level win-rate over SOTA instruction-tuned LLMs via preference-based alignment on clinical reasoning tasks
limitations_or_scope: Focused on clinical reasoning as a case study; generalizability to other expert domains (e.g., law, engineering) requires further validation.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Alfa framework decomposes 'good question' into theory-grounded attributes
evidence_spans.evidence_text: decomposing the notion of a “good” question into a set of theory-grounded attributes (e.g., clarity, relevance)

evidence_spans.claim_value: MediQ-AskDocs contains 17k clinical interactions and 80k attribute-specific preference pairs
evidence_spans.evidence_text: introduce the MediQ-AskDocs dataset, composed of 17k real-world clinical interactions augmented with 80k attribute-specific preference pairs

evidence_spans.claim_value: Alfa reduces diagnostic errors by 56.6% and achieves 64.4% question-level win-rate
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Models aligned with Alfa reduce diagnostic errors by 56.6% on MediQ-AskDocs compared to SOTA instruction-tuned LLMs, with a question-level win-rate of 64.4%

problem_statement: Text embeddings enable powerful NLP applications, but similarity scores lack transparency—users cannot explain *why* two texts are deemed similar (e.g., due to semantics, paraphrase, token overlap, or bias), hindering trust and debugging in high-stakes settings.
core_contributions: Systematic taxonomy of interpretability methods for text similarity scores: space-shaping, set-based, and attribution-based approaches
Critical comparative analysis of trade-offs across methods—e.g., fidelity vs. generalizability, custom training vs. post-hoc applicability, theoretical guarantees vs. empirical faithfulness
Argument for pluralistic interpretation: treating distinct explainability methods as complementary evidence rather than competing explanations
limitations_or_scope: Focuses exclusively on interpretability of *text similarity scores*, not general model interpretability; does not propose a new method or benchmark, but surveys and analyzes existing ones.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Systematic taxonomy of interpretability methods for text similarity scores
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We give a structured overview of interpretability methods specializing in explaining those similarity scores

evidence_spans.claim_value: Critical comparative analysis of trade-offs across methods
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Methods differ in their conceptualization of interpretability, computational cost, fidelity to input tokens... space-shaping and set-based approaches result in inherently interpretable models... attribution-based methods... generalize to arbitrary models...
Rather than competing for the best explanation... we suggest to take individual methods as independent pieces of evidence for a given phenomenon

problem_statement: Quadratic attention complexity in prefilling and excessive KV cache memory in decoding hinder efficient long-context LLM serving.
core_contributions: Introduces LServe, a unified hybrid sparse attention system for efficient long-sequence LLM serving across both prefilling and decoding stages
Proposes block-wise static + dynamic sparsity integration, converting half the attention heads into near-free 'streaming heads'
Designs a query-centric hierarchical KV page selection policy requiring only a constant number of KV pages regardless of context length
limitations_or_scope: Evaluated on A100 and L40S GPUs; focuses on decoder-only LLMs (e.g., Llama-3-8B); assumes structured sparsity compatibility with existing serving runtimes.

evidence_spans.claim_value: LServe accelerates prefilling by up to 2.9× and decoding by 1.3–2.1× over vLLM
evidence_spans.evidence_text: On average, LServe accelerates LLM prefilling by up to 2.9×\times and decoding by 1.3-2.1×\times over vLLM, maintaining long-context accuracy.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Unifies hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns for both prefilling and decoding
evidence_spans.evidence_text: This method unifies different hardware-friendly, structured sparsity patterns for both prefilling and decoding attention into a single framework

evidence_spans.claim_value: Only a constant number of KV pages is required to preserve long-context capabilities
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Additionally, we find that only a constant number of KV pages is required to preserve long-context capabilities, irrespective of context length.
